about_page_description: Audio designer, composer, and developer working with interactive music systems, game audio implementation, and real-time DSP.
about_journey_p1: My path into audio technology started with classical piano at age 6, where I learned discipline and musical structure. During high school, I discovered the mathematical beauty behind sound: how frequencies, harmonics, and digital signal processing could create entirely new sonic possibilities.
about_journey_p2: This led me to develop machine learning systems for real-time audio analysis (achieving 45ms latency), create custom DSP algorithms for spatial audio, and build interactive music systems that adapt to player behavior. At DAE Belgium, I specialized in professional game audio integration, creating audio systems that support gameplay and player immersion.
about_drives_p1: Good audio needs to work reliably and respond fast. Latency matters in real-time systems. Frequency balance matters in immersive soundscapes. I care about both the technical execution and the end result.
about_drives_p2: I build tools that solve real problems. When composers and sound designers can focus on creativity instead of fighting technical issues, that works. Real-time beat detection, adaptive music systems, audio plugins - I make complex things work smoothly.

philosophy_quote: Audio should support gameplay without getting in the way. Clarity matters more than complexity. Technical implementation and creative decisions need to work together.
principle_clarity_desc: In game audio, clarity is most important. I design from gameplay first, so critical feedback never gets masked. Mix hierarchy, frequency allocation, and dynamic ducking keep the player informed without overwhelming them.
principle_technical_desc: Understanding the technical constraints (voice counts, memory budgets, CPU limits) helps me make better creative decisions. I build systems that scale, iterate quickly, and stay performant across platforms.
principle_layering_desc: I approach sound design as modular layering: transients for impact, body for presence, texture for character. Parameters like speed, intensity, and camera distance control real-time changes, creating responsive, adaptive audio.
principle_collaboration_desc: Great audio comes from feedback loops with designers, programmers, and players. I document my work, explain technical choices, and iterate based on playtesting. Audio is never "done" until the game ships.

project_not_today_darling_short_desc: Side-scrolling 1-4 player racing game with destruction and power-ups. Solo audio designer on 6-person student team.
project_not_today_darling_full_desc: 3-layer adaptive music in Wwise. Layers change with player count and race intensity. Kept music coherent under tight voice limits.
project_amorak_short_desc: Sound design for a horror animation where a man traps a beast. Creature roar built from lion, elephant, tiger, and hippo sounds layered together.
project_nottoday_block1_content:
ROLE: Solo audio on a 6-person team. I handled everything: sourcing sounds (Soundly), processing and mixing (REAPER), building procedural systems (MetaSounds), and implementing the C++ architecture.

RESULT: Released on itch.io in May 2025. Windows and Linux builds support 2-4 players locally.
project_nottoday_block2_content:
Built entirely on MetaSounds for procedural audio. Parameters drive real-time modulation, and priority-based mixing keeps the chaos under control.

  • Speed maps to pitch multiplier (0.8x-1.3x)
  • Surface enum selects crossfaded samples
  • Collision force drives impact volume
project_shadowframes_full_desc:
A psychological horror game set in a 1960s Irish pub. Audio is not just atmospheric—it's the primary detection mechanic.

Developed in collaboration with RITCS (Narrative) and KASK Conservatory (Music). My role focused on the entire audio pipeline: from recording foley to implementing complex Wwise systems in Unreal Engine C++.
project_shadowframes_collab_desc:
• RITCS: Narrative Design & Story
• KASK Conservatory: Music Composition
• Howest DAE: Game Development & Audio Implementation
project_amorak_full_desc:
Watch how sound design builds the horror atmosphere. Every creature growl, environmental layer, and spatial detail was crafted to create immersive tension that scales dynamically with the visuals.

Key Elements:
• Creature sound signatures
• Environmental atmosphere layers
• Dynamic spatial audio mixing
• Proximity-based intensity scaling
project_amorak_block1_content: Each creature has a unique sonic identity built from organic textures, processed animal vocalizations, and synthesized sub-frequencies. The beast's presence is felt through low-frequency rumbles that scale with proximity.
project_amorak_block2_content: The basement environment uses layered ambient textures - dripping water, creaking wood, distant echoes, and subtle electrical hums. These elements dynamically respond to camera position, creating depth and spatial awareness.
project_amorak_block3_content: Strategic frequency architecture ensures clarity and impact. Creature sounds occupy 40-200Hz for body and presence. Environmental details fill mid-range. High frequencies reserved for tension-building textures.
project_gradwork_full_desc: Graduate research exploring real-time AI audio generation in games.
project_gradwork_block1_content: You might be wondering why anyone would even try to generate sounds with AI in games. What if instead of having hundreds of pre-recorded sound effects, games could create them on the fly? The main question was: Is AI fast enough that players wouldn't even notice the delay?
project_gradwork_block2_content: I expected latency. I didn't expect 12,000 ms. In a game running at 60 FPS, a footstep needs to happen in 16 milliseconds. My first attempt was 750 times too slow. Even the faster MusicGen model took 4 seconds. In the world of game development, 4 seconds is an eternity.
project_gradwork_block3_content: If we can't generate sound in real-time, we have to generate it before it happens. I built a system that uses the loading screen to 'hallucinate' the audio for the level ahead. By the time the player spawns, the AI has already done the heavy lifting. The result? Zero latency.
project_transientica_block1_content:
Transientica is not just a simple volume trigger. It uses Machine Learning to understand what sound you are making.

Each person's voice is different. A kick drum might sound like a deep 'Boom' for one person and a punchy 'Puh' for another. The system trains on your specific microphone input in real-time to build a custom profile.
project_transientica_block2_content:
Spectral Analysis

Kick drums are deep (low frequency energy), snares have noise (high frequency spread). I trained the system to recognize these spectral fingerprints along with temporal envelopes (how fast the sound starts and stops).

Optimization Strategy

To achieve <45ms latency (critical for rhythm games), I had to bypass Unity's garbage collector constraints.

  • Circular Buffer: Eliminates memory allocation during recording.
  • Thread Separation: Audio analysis happens on a high-priority thread, UI on the main thread.
  • OSC Communication: Decoupled Python ML inference from the game engine using UDP packets.
project_pause_and_deserve_short_desc: Psychological horror game with strategic pause mechanics.
project_pause_and_deserve_full_desc:
Psychological horror game where every pause comes with a price.

I designed a reactive audio system in Unity where the soundscape shifts based on the player's hesitation. The 'Pause' mechanic isn't just UI—it triggers time-manipulation audio effects, pitch-shifting downward and extending reverb tails to build dread.
project_interactive_music_short_desc: Adaptive audio systems with vertical layering in Wwise.
project_interactive_music_full_desc: Wwise music system with vertical layering and dynamic mixing. Adapts to gameplay intensity and player actions. Fits in memory budget.
project_audioq_full_desc:
JUCE-based audio sampler with granular synthesis, tremolo effects, and professional DSP processing.

Features:
- Granular Synthesis: Adjustable grain size and random playback.
- Custom Tremolo: Per-sample LFO amplitude modulation.
- Filter System: TPT (Topology-Preserving Transform) filters for zero-delay.
- APVTS: Full parameter automation support.

Technical Details:
- Circular Buffer Implementation
- FFT Windowing (Hanning)
- Lock-free Parameter Updates (APVTS)
- Custom Look-and-Feel GUI
